article.title: How to Edge a Flower Bed (Clean Natural Edge)
article.summary: Cut a crisp, natural edge between lawn and flower bed with a spade: mark the line, cut a vertical edge, bevel the bed side, then mulch and maintain.
article.body:
A clean edge between lawn and bed makes a whole yard look cared for, and it slows grass from creeping into the bed. A natural spade-cut edge costs nothing but time. This guide covers new beds and overgrown edges.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear sturdy shoes. Call 811 a few days before digging so buried utility lines can be marked, even for shallow edging.

Steps

  1. Mark the line

    Lay a garden hose along the edge you want, adjusting it until curves look smooth from the house and street. Mark it with marking paint or by cutting a shallow line with the edger along the hose.

    Done right: the line has smooth, deliberate curves and no awkward kinks.

  2. Cut a vertical edge on the lawn side

    Stand on the lawn side. Push the half-moon edger or spade straight down about 3 to 4 in deep along the line, overlapping each cut slightly. Keep the blade vertical so the lawn edge stays crisp.

    Done right: a continuous vertical cut runs the full length of the line.

  3. Bevel the bed side

    From the bed side, cut at about a 45-degree angle toward the bottom of your vertical cut, making a V-shaped trench. Lift out the wedge of sod and soil.

    Done right: a clean V-trench, about 3 to 4 in deep, separates lawn from bed.

  4. Tidy up and mulch

    Shake soil from the removed sod back into the bed, and compost or discard the grass. Rake the bed smooth and spread 2 to 3 in of mulch, keeping its top just below the edge and away from plant stems.

    Done right: the mulch sits below the lawn edge, so the line stays visible.

  5. Maintain the edge

    Recut the vertical edge with the edger or a string trimmer turned on its side every few weeks in the growing season. Light, frequent touch-ups keep it sharp.

    Done right: grass isn't growing over the trench a month later.

Hire a landscaper if: you want stone, brick or steel edging set in concrete, the beds are on a steep slope, or the yard has extensive tree roots along the edge.

FAQ

How deep should a flower bed edge be?

About 3 to 4 in deep is enough to stop most lawn grass runners.

What tool is best for edging flower beds?

A half-moon edger makes clean, curved cuts. A flat spade also works well.

How often should I re-edge my beds?

Touch up the edge every few weeks during the growing season to keep it crisp.

Should mulch be higher than the edge?

No. Keep mulch just below the lawn edge so the line stays visible and mulch doesn't spill onto the grass.
